summary:
FOURTEEN PAIRS DECLARED, ALL FOURTEEN DRIVEN THROUGH THE REAL spine.assemble.build IN A FRESH SUBPROCESS PER CELL, AND THE ONE THING THE CLASSIFICATION GOT WRONG IS THE HI END ON THE THREE COSINE DISTANCES.

THE HEADLINE. DOM_SHIFT_DIST, DOM_SPAWN_DIST and DOM_MERGE_DIST are declared `cosine distance` and every reader compares them against 1 - cosine_similarity between UNIT vectors, which runs on [0, 2]. They get domain=(0.0, 2.0). A reflexive (0.0, 1.0) taken from the U.FRACTION column would have REFUSED 1.24 -- a pooled radius this tree MEASURED, on this geometry, and records in my own file at radius_cap as '1.24 of a maximum possible 2.0'. It would have been Fact 3 committed in the hi direction: refusing a reading the mechanism produces. Corroborated without contact: the FAB owner, editing concurrently, reached (0.0, 2.0) on their two cosine-distance levers independently.

THE OTHER ELEVEN ARE (0.0, 1.0), AND NOT ONE OF THE ARGUMENTS IS THE UNIT COLUMN. Two are quantile POINTS (DOM_SHIFT_Q, DOM_RADIUS_Q -- the old body hands DOM_RADIUS_Q straight to torch.quantile, which I drove: q=1.5 and q=-0.1 both RuntimeError, naming neither lever nor value). Two are RETENTION MULTIPLIERS whose hi end is a declared no-op arm (DOM_DECAY's 1.0 is the cumulative-forever regime it replaced; DOM_TOKC_DECAY's 1.0 is named in the help string; MEM_USE_DECAY's 1.0 is the `use_decay < 1.0` guard the body already carries). One is a CONVEX MIXTURE WEIGHT (DOM_PRIOR_BLEND: (1-w)*p_model + w*p_prior leaves the simplex outside [0,1]). Three are SHARES OF A CONTAINER (DOM_CULL_FRAC of the live population, MEM_PROBATION_FRAC of the owner's block, MEM_WRITE_TARGET of the offered writes). Two are THRESHOLDS ON A QUANTITY WHOSE OWN RANGE IS [0,1] (MEM_WRITE_GATE on surprise = 1 - p_model; MEM_PRESSURE_THRESH on main/(main+prob), a share of a partition).

ZERO WAS CHECKED FROM THE API BODY, NOT THE DECLARATION, exactly as Fact 4 says it has to be. DOM_CULL_FRAC=0 is a legitimate empty budget declared ONLY as the counter name n_cull_budget_zero in src/domains/api.py::manage's DID IT FIRE list -- there is no sentence for it anywhere else -- and DOM_PRIOR_BLEND=0 is the off-switch src/domains/api.py::prior returns (None, 0.0) for. lo=0.0 admits both. None of my 14 has a negative natural low end, and the two levers that do (EVAL_GENUINE_SIL, MEM_MATCH_FLOOR) are not on my list. THE NEGATIVE SIDE IS WHERE TWO OF THESE PAIRS EARN THEIR KEEP, measured: DOM_CULL_FRAC=-0.1 makes int(-0.1*n) NEGATIVE, so at n=10 the budget slice order[:-1] is NINE of the ten domains instead of one; DOM_SHIFT_Q=-0.1 indexes v[-51] of a 512-sample sorted window, i.e. the 0.90 quantile answering a request for a low base.

PROOF, BOTH DIRECTIONS, EVERY CELL RUN AND PASTED. Per lever: the shipped default with the variable unset, both endpoints, a value just below lo, a value just above hi, two ordinary interior values, and nan/inf/-inf/1e26. 14 x ~11 cells, each in a fresh subprocess through spine.assemble.build(os.environ). Every refusal names the lever and the value. AND THE DOMAIN'S OWN CONTRIBUTION ISOLATED: with REFUSE_NON_FINITE_FLOAT flipped False in a copy of src/ OUTSIDE the repository, all 42 non-finite cells (14 levers x nan/inf/-inf) are still refused, by the pair -- 42 of the 69 UNREACHABLE_TODAY float cells the domains-memory sweep filed.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT BUY, DRIVEN RATHER THAN DISCLAIMED. Every value the tree's own record calls wrong is inside its pair and still builds: DOM_MERGE_DIST=0.12 (8x fragmentation) and =0.80 (the counterfeit 4, purity 0.71) both resolve; DOM_SHIFT_DIST=0.30 is the constant whose boundary precision fell 0.92 -> 0.27; MEM_PRESSURE_THRESH=0.80 is exactly unreachable on this tree because n_promoted is identically 0. These are bounds on a SPELLING. No comment I wrote calls any lever safe, bounded or validated, and five of them say in as many words what the pair cannot reach.

THE REGRESSION I CAUSED IS ONE DRIFTED LINE SPAN AND IT IS THE DRIFT N8 EXISTS FOR. My comments pushed `wrong_sweep` in src/memory/levers.py from line 463 to 517, so tests/test_census.py's DEPARTURES `where` (:463-475) now opens on another lever. tests/ is not mine: the exact find/replace (-> :517-529) is in unfinished and I VERIFIED it in a copy of the tree, where census returns to 8 checks + the self-test, 0 failing. I did not move or delete a comment to keep a line number true. One further citation drifted in docs/04_CONTRACT.md (domains/levers.py:615 -> :700), also filed. THE OTHER SUITE FAILURE IS NOT MINE AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN CLAIMING IT: test_fabric F4 broke mid-run when a concurrent owner declared domain=(0.0, 2.0) on FAB_DISCOVER, which pre-empts the read-site refusal F4 asserts is FAB's. findings.item: THE HEADLINE, AND THE ONE PLACE THE CLASSIFICATION'S HI END WAS WRONG: DOM_SHIFT_DIST, DOM_SPAWN_DIST and DOM_MERGE_DIST are COSINE DISTANCES and get (0.0, 2.0), not (0.0, 1.0)
findings.detail: All three declarations say `cosine distance` in the help string, and the quantity every reader compares them against is 1 - cosine_similarity between two UNIT vectors, which runs on [0, 2]. Writing 1.0 because the unit column says FRACTION would be Fact 3 committed in the hi direction: it would REFUSE readings this geometry actually produces, which is the one direction of error spine/lever.py's own declaration comment says a domain must never make. THE EVIDENCE IS IN MY OWN FILE AND IT IS MEASURED, not argued: src/domains/levers.py's radius_cap comment records a pooled radius observed at 1.24 of a maximum possible 2.0 -- a distance ABOVE 1.0 on this exact geometry, after a real collapse -- and the old body's own sentinel for 'below every possible similarity' is M.fill_diagonal_(-2.0), i.e. the author already treats similarity as reaching -1 and distance as reaching 2. The spawn_dist comment's own probe series reaches .668 and is still climbing at the last measured point. Both ends are settings rather than typos: at 0.0 shift_dist trips on every window and spawn_dist spawns on every assign; at 2.0 no jump can exceed the threshold, so shift_dist never fires (the documented inert-partition path this group's banner already names) and spawn_dist never spawns; merge_dist at 2.0 collapses the population to one domain. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, unplanned: while I was working, the FAB owner declared the same (0.0, 2.0) on their two cosine-distance levers (src/fabric/levers.py lines with FAB_DISCOVER and the route/merge distance) -- two readers, same conclusion, no contact.

The 1.24 cell is the point: under a reflexive (0.0, 1.0) all three of those would have been REFUSED, and 1.24 is a number this tree measured rather than imagined.
Source of the range, read not assumed: self_organize.py's DomainAssembler.update computes `d = 1 - F.cosine_similarity(sig.unsqueeze(0), s.run_sig.unsqueeze(0)).item()`; rekey computes `di = 1 - zi @ c` and the Voronoi guard `M.fill_diagonal_(-2.0)` then `_nn = 1 - M.max(1).values`.

findings.item: SECOND READER'S VERDICT ON THE LIST ITSELF: all 14 belong; three needed a different HI end and none needed to be dropped
findings.detail: I read every one of the 14 declarations and every reader of it -- the frozen contract in the owning api.py, and the body it is ported from -- before writing a pair. The classification is right that both ends are derivable on all 14. It is wrong only about WHICH high end on the three cosine distances (finding 1). On the other eleven the hi is 1.0 and the argument is never the unit column: two are quantile POINTS (the q of a quantile is defined on [0,1] and nothing else), two are RETENTION MULTIPLIERS whose hi end is a declared no-op arm, one is a CONVEX MIXTURE WEIGHT, three are SHARES OF A CONTAINER, one is a SETPOINT ON A RATIO OF NESTED COUNTERS, and two are THRESHOLDS ON A QUANTITY WHOSE OWN RANGE IS [0,1] (a probability complement; a share of a partition). NOTE ON THE BRIEF'S WARNING: FAB_HALT_MAX is not on my list -- my 14 are the nine DOM and five MEM levers named in my task, and I did not add to or subtract from them. ZERO WAS CHECKED PER LEVER, NOT ASSUMED: lo=0.0 on all 14, and on the two where 0 is a DECLARED state I learned it from the api body exactly as Fact 4 says I would have to -- DOM_CULL_FRAC's empty budget is declared only as the counter name n_cull_budget_zero in src/domains/api.py::manage's DID IT FIRE list (there is no sentence for it in the declaration), and DOM_PRIOR_BLEND=0 is the off-switch src/domains/api.py::prior returns (None, 0.0) for. Both are also in the domains-memory sweep's legitimate_specials block, which I read. NEITHER OF THE TWO GENUINELY-NEGATIVE LEVERS (EVAL_GENUINE_SIL, MEM_MATCH_FLOOR) is on my list, and none of my 14 has a negative natural low end: a cosine DISTANCE, a quantile point, a share, a retention factor and a probability threshold are all floored at 0 by what they measure.
findings.repro: Per-lever reading recorded in the 14 declaration comments, each citing its reader in path/file.py::symbol form (O13 opens all of them: ownership 13 checks + 43 self-test cases, 0 failing, after the edit). The zero evidence: `grep -n n_cull_budget_zero src/domains/api.py` -> in manage's DID IT FIRE list; src/domains/api.py::prior: 'Returns (probs, weight), or (None, 0.0) when prior_blend == 0'; .rework/audits/sweep_domains-memory.json legitimate_specials names DOM_CULL_FRAC=0 and DOM_PRIOR_BLEND=0 with their declaration sites.

findings.item: DOM_SHIFT_DIST -- domain=(0.0, 2.0) declared, default 0.30 inside it
findings.detail: An adjacent-window cosine distance compared by src/domains/api.py::observe. See finding 1 for the range. 0.0 = every window is over threshold; 2.0 = no jump can exceed it, the never-fires arm.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.3 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 2.0 -> 2.0 | 0.5 -> 0.5 | 1.24 -> 1.24 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 2.0] | 2.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 2.0] | 1e26 REFUSED [0.0, 2.0]

findings.item: DOM_SHIFT_Q -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.50 inside it
findings.detail: A QUANTILE POINT: src/domains/api.py::observe takes it over the last 512 adjacent distances, and a quantile is defined on [0, 1] -- 0.0 the smallest recent distance, 1.0 the largest, both bases a calibration would pick. THE NEGATIVE SIDE IS A MEASURED SILENT WRONG ANSWER, not a style point: the body indexes v[min(len-1, int(shift_q*len))], so on a full 512-sample window shift_q=-0.1 resolves to v[-51] = the 0.90 quantile -- a request for a LOW base answered with a high one, with nothing printed. shift_mult, its partner, deliberately gets NO pair: it is a multiple of that base and no ceiling is derivable for it.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.5 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.75 -> 0.75 | 0.9 -> 0.9 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. Index arithmetic driven: v=list(range(512)); min(511, int(-0.1*512)) = -51; v[-51] = 461, i.e. quantile 0.902.

findings.item: DOM_RADIUS_Q -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.85 inside it
findings.detail: The q of a quantile, and the reader is the operation itself: src/domains/api.py::rekey takes it over one domain's reservoir distances and again over ALL domains' distances for the pooled radius. Off [0, 1] a quantile selects nothing -- the old body handed it straight to torch.quantile, which refuses out-of-range q with a RuntimeError naming neither lever nor value. 0.0 is the nearest reservoir sample, 1.0 the furthest.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.85 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.5 -> 0.5 | 0.95 -> 0.95 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. torch.quantile driven directly: q=0.0 -> 0.1, q=1.0 -> 0.4, q=1.5 -> RuntimeError 'quantile() q must be in the range [0, 1] but got 1.5', q=-0.1 -> the same, q=nan -> the same.

findings.detail: 1 - cos between two centroids, compared by src/domains/api.py::manage. See finding 1. 0.0 merges only centroids that coincide exactly (merge off in everything but name); 2.0 collapses the population to one domain.

And the two settings the tree's own sweep prices as WRONG both still build, which is the point of the next finding: 0.12 -> 0.12, 0.80 -> 0.8.

findings.item: DOM_CULL_FRAC -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.10 inside it
findings.detail: A share of the live population: src/domains/api.py::manage takes int(cull_frac * n) domains off the bottom of the activity order. 1.0 considers the whole population and there is nothing above it to name. LO=0.0 IS LEARNED FROM THE api BODY, not the declaration: the empty budget is anticipated by name as the counter n_cull_budget_zero, and this lever's entire history is a max(1, ...) floor that ratcheted a population to a single domain, so 0 is the direction that loses nothing. THE NEGATIVE SIDE IS WHAT THE PAIR EARNS: the budget is a list slice, so int(-0.1 * n) is negative and Python reads it from the other end -- at n = 10 the budget becomes order[:-1], NINE of the ten domains instead of one.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.1 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.5 -> 0.5 | 0.01 -> 0.01 | -0.1 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. Slice arithmetic driven on a 10-domain order: frac=0.10 -> ['a']; frac=-0.1 -> int(-1.0) = -1 -> ['a'..'i'] (9 of 10); frac=1.0 -> all ten.

findings.item: DOM_DECAY -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.9 inside it
findings.detail: A retention multiplier: src/domains/api.py::manage multiplies `act` by it once per pass, so it is the fraction of a counter that survives. 1.0 keeps all of it and is exactly the cumulative regime this lever replaced, under which a domain that ever reached the minimum was immortal -- a real arm, and refusing it would refuse the behaviour rather than the mistake. 0.0 makes `act` the activity of the last pass alone. Above 1.0 it is a GAIN: `act` compounds, cull_act_min is never reached again and the cull's activity conjunct is dead while every counter still prints.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.9 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.5 -> 0.5 | 0.99 -> 0.99 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED

findings.item: DOM_PRIOR_BLEND -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.15 inside it
findings.detail: The weight of a CONVEX mixture -- (1 - prior_blend) * p_model + prior_blend * p_prior -- so outside [0, 1] one of the two distributions enters with a negative weight and the result is off the simplex. 0.0 is the declared off-switch on both of this field's jobs (help string, and src/domains/api.py::prior returns (None, 0.0) at 0), so lo must admit it; 1.0 is the histogram alone, the ablation the domain-prior table needs.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.15 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.5 -> 0.5 | 0.85 -> 0.85 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. The convex form read, not assumed: self_organize.py's eval blend is `_q = _pm if mix is None else (1 - DOM_PRIOR) * _pm + DOM_PRIOR * mix.unsqueeze(1)`.

findings.item: DOM_TOKC_DECAY -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.5 inside it
findings.detail: `decay`'s argument on the other histogram: src/domains/api.py::on_retokenize multiplies every count by it once per retok. The HI end is declared in the help string rather than chosen by me -- 1.0 restores cumulative-forever -- and 0.0 drops the pre-retok counts outright, the strict reading of the argument that they are observations of a different distribution. Above 1.0 the counts are amplified at an event that supplies no new observations.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.5 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.25 -> 0.25 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED

findings.item: MEM_WRITE_GATE -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.3 inside it
findings.detail: The range of the QUANTITY it is compared against, which is also the argument the declaration already makes for the U.PROBABILITY unit: src/memory/api.py::write gates a row on surprise = 1 - p_model(true token), a probability complement, which cannot leave [0, 1]. A threshold outside that interval is a comparison against a reading that cannot occur: above 1.0 nothing is ever stored, below 0.0 everything is -- and 0.0 already spells that, since the test is `>=`. Both ends are configurations: 0.0 store-every-candidate, 1.0 keeps only a token the model gave no mass at all.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.3 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.12 -> 0.12 | 0.95 -> 0.95 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. The comparison read, not assumed: memory.py's _gate does `keep = sd >= self.write_gate` with sd the surprise tensor.

findings.item: MEM_WRITE_TARGET -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.5 inside it
findings.detail: Both readers inside src/memory/api.py::write fix the same interval from opposite directions. As the controller setpoint it is a share of the offered writes to keep, and the kept fraction it is compared against is n_writes_committed / n_writes_offered -- a ratio of two counters where the first counts a subset of the second. In the quantile arm the point taken is 1 - write_target, which must land in [0, 1] for a quantile to exist. The old body reached the same interval by CLAMPING the quantile point into it at the call, which converts an out-of-range request into a silent in-range one instead of naming the lever.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.5 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.12 -> 0.12 | 0.88 -> 0.88 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. The clamp read, not assumed: memory.py's quantile arm does `q = torch.quantile(sd.float().flatten(), max(0.0, min(1.0, 1.0 - self.gate_target)))`.

findings.item: MEM_USE_DECAY -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.98 inside it
findings.detail: The HI end is not my judgement -- it is the guard the body this declaration already cites carries: the decay pass runs only while use_decay < 1.0. So 1.0 is the never-decay arm, and every value above it is that same arm spelled as a multiplier that never multiplies (1.5 and 1.0 do exactly the same nothing, and only one spelling admits it). 0.0 zeroes every retrieval count at the interval. Above 1.0 the rule runs backwards: `use` is the ranking key src/memory/api.py::write evicts on under evict="usage", and a factor above 1 compounds it, so an early-run burst grows every interval instead of fading -- the immortal entry the declaration says this multiplier exists to prevent.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.98 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.5 -> 0.5 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.5 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. The guard read, not assumed: memory.py's _commit does `if self.use_decay < 1.0 and self._wc >= self.decay_every: self.use *= self.use_decay`.

findings.item: MEM_PROBATION_FRAC -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.10 inside it
findings.detail: A share of a container, so it cannot exceed the container: src/memory/api.py::write compares the probation population against this share of the OWNER'S BLOCK, and the never-retrieved region is a SUBSET of that block. A share above 1.0 names a region larger than the thing it is a region of and behaves identically to 1.0. Both ends are arms: at 0.0 the region is over budget the moment it is non-empty, so eviction always narrows to probation; at 1.0 it never narrows and eviction falls through to whatever `evict` ranks on -- the ablation the scan-resistance claim is scored against.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.1 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.25 -> 0.25 | 0.82 -> 0.82 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. The comparison read, not assumed: memory.py does `_over = _pn > int(self.prob_frac * self.cap)` with _pn = int(self.prob.sum()), so at 1.0 `>` can never hold.

findings.item: MEM_PRESSURE_THRESH -- domain=(0.0, 1.0) declared, default 0.80 inside it
findings.detail: The comparand is a share of a partition: src/memory/api.py::census forms pressure as main/(main + prob) over eviction BRANCHES, two counters that partition the evictions, so the reading lies in [0, 1] and a threshold outside it either can never be crossed or can never not be. Both endpoints are live readings rather than edge cases -- that same function records pinned-at-0 and pinned-at-1 as the two outcomes a fed probe could produce.
findings.repro: Fresh subprocess per cell, real spine.assemble.build(os.environ): <unset> -> 0.8 | 0.0 -> 0.0 | 1.0 -> 1.0 | 0.5 -> 0.5 | 0.95 -> 0.95 | -0.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1.0001 REFUSED [0.0, 1.0] | 1e26 REFUSED. The formula read, not assumed: memory.py's pressure() returns `self.n_main_evict / tot` with `tot = self.n_prob_evict + self.n_main_evict`, and the old comparison is `_pr >= _f('MEM_PRESSURE', 0.80)`, so 1.0 is reachable.

findings.item: WHAT THE 14 PAIRS ADD THAT THE FINITENESS FLOOR DOES NOT: 42 non-finite cells refused BY THE DECLARATION ALONE, with the central floor switched off
findings.detail: On the shipped tree nan/inf/-inf on these levers are refused by spine/lever.py::REFUSE_NON_FINITE_FLOAT, so the domain's own contribution is invisible. I isolated it the way d_lever's section H did: copied src/ to a scratch tree OUTSIDE the repository, set REFUSE_NON_FINITE_FLOAT = False there only, and drove all 14 levers at nan, inf and -inf. All 42 cells are refused by the DOMAIN, naming the lever and the value. That is the inverted-chain comparison doing its work (`not lo <= v`), plus a finite HIGH end on all 14 -- these are not open-topped levers, so +inf is refused here too. The two rules are still complements and not alternatives: hi=None on some OTHER lever would admit +inf, which is why the floor exists; on these 14 the pair happens to cover the same cells from the other side. AGAINST THE SWEEP: sweep_domains-memory.json filed 69 UNREACHABLE_TODAY cells as '23 float levers x {nan, inf, -inf}'. 42 of those 69 are my 14 levers, and they are now refused at declaration whatever the central switch is set to.
findings.repro:
